title: Normalization of the global boundary of the pro-etale support triangle
statement:
Fix a finite commutative ring $A$. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of schemes with quasi-compact complementary open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Work with ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] and their derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with exact $i_*$ and $i^*,j^*$ as in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Put $i^!_0M=i^*\ker(M\to j_*j^*M)$ [def-pur-flasque-support], and write $S=Ri^!_0$ on $D^+$, with its support counit $\epsilon:i_*SK\to K$ as in [lem-pur-support-localization-triangle]. Let $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, represented by a bounded-below complex of injective module sheaves $I$. Let $\beta:Rj_*j^*K\to(i_*SK)[1]$ be the third arrow of the support triangle constructed from this injective resolution with the cone convention [def-pur-support-triangle, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Derived global sections identify that entire triangle with
$$R\Gamma_Z(X,K)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(X,K)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(U,j^*K)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_Z(X,K)[1],$$
where the first term is identified by the sectionwise support kernel and the third by the direct-image/sections comparison. More precisely, the sequence of complexes of $A$-modules
$$0\to\Gamma_Z(X,I)\to I(X)\to(j^*I)(U)\to0$$
is degreewise short exact, $j^*I$ computes $j^*K$, and its usual cochain connecting homomorphism equals $H^q(R\Gamma(X,\beta))$ under these identifications. For every $q\in\mathbf Z$, a cocycle $c\in(j^*I)^q(U)$ and a lift $b\in I^q(X)$, that homomorphism sends $[c]$ to $[db]\in H^{q+1}(\Gamma_Z(X,I))$. Thus it is precisely the supported-cohomology boundary $\partial$ of [thm-pur-with-support-exactness], with no extra sign. These identifications and the boundary are natural in $K$.

proof.text: The ringed-site module kernel-comparison lemma gives enough injectives in $\operatorname{Mod}(A_X)$. Apply the injective support-row lemma to the given $i,j,A,I$. It gives the actual supported-kernel inclusion, the sheaf row and its short exact section row, as well as the injective representatives of all three derived objects. In particular $j^*I$ represents $j^*K$, and the sectionwise kernel and direct-image identifications fix the first and third global objects and the first two maps.

proof.text: Apply the derived cone-comparison lemma with $T=\Gamma(X,-)$ to this sheaf row. Its hypotheses hold by step 1, including exactness of the section row. The support localization theorem identifies the sheaf cone triangle with the specified support triangle. The unit-normalized comparison then identifies its entire derived-global triangle with the section-row triangle; its third arrow is $(-\operatorname{pr}_{\Gamma_Z(X,I)})q_X^{-1}$, with $q_X(b,a)=v_X(b)$. This also fixes the direct-image/sections comparison on the third term.

proof.text: Use the cone-boundary descent lemma with $\mathcal C=\operatorname{Mod}(A_X)$, $S=\Gamma_Z(X,-)$, $F=\Gamma(X,-)$ and $G=\Gamma(U,j^*(-))$. Step 1 applied to each injective sheaf in degree zero verifies exactness on injectives. The lemma identifies the third arrow of step 2 with the derived injective snake boundary and gives $[c]\mapsto[db]$ for every integer degree and every lift, with no extra sign. The supported-cohomology exactness theorem supplies $\partial$ for precisely this kernel/restriction row, so this is its boundary. The natural row identifications of step 1 and the natural triangle comparison of step 2, together with the descent lemma for chain maps modulo homotopy, give naturality in every derived morphism $K\to K\prime$ and independence of the injective resolution.

lean.note: The complete node is stated by supportGlobalTriangleComparison, supportGlobalBoundaryNormalization and supportGlobalComparisonNatural. The triangle comparison fixes every component by the right-derived unit and the sectionwise kernel/restriction squares; its final equality identifies its homology boundary with the usual snake boundary. The boundary theorem uses the existing SupportSequenceBoundary and SupportSequenceExact interfaces for every finite commutative coefficient ring, and quantifies all integer degrees, all injective representatives, all identifications with K, and all cocycle lifts. The real-data open-evaluation and derived-composition isomorphisms identify the third term with RΓ(U,j^*K).
